content:
President Donald Trump has said he is inclined to order major new military strikes against Iran after the New Year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement, raising the prospect of a fresh round of large-scale combat in a war that has already run for nearly nine months.

In exclusive comments to Fox News on Sunday, Trump said indirect talks with Tehran were still under way but dismissed them as going nowhere. "They're more aggressive now than before the election," he told Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst, describing Iranian negotiators as "professional tap dancers" who stall while continuing to escalate hostilities. "They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it's all b------," he added, according to Fox News.

The remarks, reported by [Fox News](https://foxnews.com/politics/trump-warns-new-strikes-against-iran-after-new-year-calls-negotiators-professional-tap-dancers), mark the sharpest deadline Trump has set since the fighting began. He has not announced a final decision, and in separate comments last week he said he was in no hurry, telling reporters, "We'll see what happens after January 1." But Sunday's interview is the first time he has said plainly that he leans toward resuming major strikes if diplomacy fails by that date.

Trump has repeatedly insisted that any agreement must permanently prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, and in an earlier Fox News interview he said he wanted a deal that would still bind future American presidents. The problem, as his own administration's critics and supporters alike acknowledge, is that no such guarantee exists in American law: an executive agreement can be abandoned by the next president, as Trump himself did with the 2015 nuclear deal in 2018, while a treaty would need two-thirds of the Senate, a threshold that looks unreachable in the current Congress. That legal gap is one reason the talks have stalled, and why the threat of renewed force now carries more weight than the promise of a deal.

The president also used the interview to dare Tehran to test the American naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iranian state media reported this week that Iranian vessels could try to break through the blockade, and Trump answered bluntly: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy." He indicated that American forces would open fire on any vessel attempting to breach it. The warning comes days after Tehran said it was assembling a convoy of 14 oil tankers to challenge the blockade, a move Washington has called a provocation. For the background on that standoff, see our earlier report on the [Iranian tanker convoy](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/ar/articles/iran-14-tanker-convoy-break-us-blockade-november-2026).

The military balance behind the threats is formidable on both sides. Two American aircraft carrier strike groups are operating in the Arabian Sea, with aerial refuelling aircraft positioned in Israel, according to Fox News. Yet Iran has kept fighting through months of American operations. The United States launched Operation Epic Fury on February 28, striking Iranian military targets and killing senior officials, but Tehran has continued to launch attacks across the region. According to figures reported by The Wall Street Journal and cited by The Jerusalem Post, Iran still holds around 1,500 ballistic missiles and can manufacture roughly 50 more each month.

The tit-for-tat pattern has continued into this week. Fox News reported overnight attacks on American forces in Bahrain, and on Saturday an Iranian strike hit a civilian industrial facility in the Gulf state. Iran's Revolutionary Guard has claimed the downing of American drones over the Strait of Hormuz, while oil tankers have been hit by mines and projectiles near Oman's Khasab coast. The US Senate, meanwhile, voted 51 to 48 on Thursday to reject a war-powers resolution that would have forced Trump to end the campaign or seek congressional approval, leaving the president's authority to order new strikes unchallenged for now. The vote is covered in our report on the [Senate's war-powers decision](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/ar/articles/us-senate-rejects-iran-war-powers-resolution-november-2026).

Trump also turned to the unrest inside Iran, where anti-government demonstrations have flared again in several cities amid rolling electricity outages announced by the authorities. Asked about the protests, he offered a direct message to demonstrators: "Keep protesting." It was the most explicit encouragement he has given to the protest movement since the war began, and it adds a domestic pressure point to the military and economic squeeze on Tehran.

America's Gulf allies, meanwhile, are pressing hard in the opposite direction. Governments across the region fear that renewed American strikes would trigger another wave of Iranian retaliation against their territory and energy infrastructure, as happened in the early stages of Operation Epic Fury, when Gulf states came under Iranian missile and drone attacks. Qatar continues to act as the intermediary, carrying messages between Washington and Tehran in an effort to reach an agreement, and Trump has acknowledged the importance of Doha's role.

For now, Washington is caught between two tracks that point in opposite directions: a negotiation that the president himself calls meaningless, and a military option he says he is inclined to use. What happens after January 1 will depend on whether the indirect talks, mediated by Qatar, produce anything in the next five weeks, or whether the deadline Trump has now set publicly becomes the starting point for a new phase of the war. The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world's oil passes, remains the most exposed flashpoint, and shipping and energy markets will be watching every signal from both capitals as the year ends.
summary: President Donald Trump told Fox News he is inclined to order major new strikes against Iran after the New Year if talks fail, calling Iranian negotiators "professional tap dancers" and warning that any vessel testing the US naval blockade would be sunk, while urging Iranian protesters to keep demonstrating.
title: Trump 'inclined' to resume major strikes on Iran after New Year if talks fail
